videos.title: Careless Influences & The Danger of Neglect | Righteousness Series | Dave Coke
videos.description:
Are you living carelessly toward God? In this powerful message from his Righteousness series, Pastor Dave Coke examines the spirit of carelessness — what it is, how it creeps in, and what Scripture says about those who neglect the things of God.
Using the vivid Old Testament account of Esau selling his birthright for a bowl of stew, Pastor Dave shows how trading eternal things for momentary comfort is one of the most dangerous traps a believer can fall into.
📖 In this message you'll discover:
    • What carelessness really means — and why it's more dangerous than most sins people worry about 
    • How Hebrews 2:2–3 warns us about neglecting so great a salvation 
    • The story of Esau (Genesis 25:27–34) as a vivid example of a careless person in Scripture 
    • Why emotions are not sin — but carelessness with them can lead to sin 
    • How to keep pleasure in its proper perspective without becoming legalistic 
    • The sobering truth: some things lost through carelessness cannot be regained 
    • Leviticus 19:17 — the timeless principle of rebuking without hatred 
📚 Key Scriptures Referenced: Isaiah 35:8 • Hebrews 2:2–3 • Genesis 25:27–34 • 1 Corinthians 10:13 • John 6:27 • Leviticus 19:17
🕊️ About Living Faith Church: Located in Rockton, Illinois, this was the church of the late Pastor Dave Coke. Today, Brother Bill serves as the current pastor, continuing the mission of preaching Holiness unto the Lord.

videos.title: Persecution & Glorification: The Final Steps of Salvation | Pastor Dave Coke | Living Faith Church
videos.description:
In this concluding message of his multi-part salvation series, Pastor Dave Coke walks through the final two steps of salvation — Persecution and Glorification. Drawing from Romans 13, Romans 8, Acts 7, Acts 14, Revelation 2, and 1 John 3, Pastor Dave delivers a straight-talking, scripture-saturated message on what it truly means to endure to the end, why suffering for the gospel is a sign of righteous living, and what awaits the saints in glorification.
If you've been told salvation is a one-time prayer with no ongoing cost — this message will challenge everything you think you know. Salvation is not complete until you have been resurrected and glorified. And the road there runs straight through persecution.

🔥 Highlights:
    • Father's Day reflections: Why being a father — not a friend — to your children is one of the most important things a man can do, and why the model for all fatherhood is God the Father Himself 
    • Step 8 — Persecution: The saint lives righteously and will be persecuted. The three agents of persecution — sinners trying to silence a witness that convicts them, fellow religious people (the most common source), and the Godhead who takes persecution of Christians personally — "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?" (Acts 9:4) 
    • Stephen in Acts 7: Why they couldn't refute his logic so they killed the witness instead — and why the same dynamic plays out on every campus and in every workplace today 
    • Romans 8:16–17: The biggest little word — if indeed we suffer with Him. The sobering implication: unwillingness to suffer any embarrassment for Christ may be a sign you are not yet His child 
    • Acts 14:21–22: "Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God" — not a few, many. Persecution is not the exception for the believer, it is the rule 
    • Revelation 2:10: "Be faithful until death and I will give you the crown of life" — why God does not simply remove persecution, and why we should thank Him for counting us worthy to bear it 
      
    • Step 9 — Glorification: Truth tested becomes truth fulfilled. Salvation is not complete until resurrection and glorification. You are like Jesus morally at conversion and materially at resurrection 
    • 1 John 3:2–3: "Everyone who has this hope purifies himself, just as He is pure" — you won't be like Him physically unless you are like Him morally 
    • Free will in eternity: Why you will never lose your free will in heaven — and why losing it would make praise, worship, and virtue meaningless. God tests us here so there are no more Lucifer incidents in eternity 
    • Heaven as endless exploration: The knowledge of God is inexhaustible — eternity is an endless discovery of the greatness of God, and He may create whole new universes for us to explore

videos.title: What Should You Be Laboring For? A Biblical View of Work, Wealth & True Riches | Pastor Dave Coke
videos.description:
Labor Day is celebrated as a day off — but what does the Bible actually say about work, wealth, and what we should truly be laboring for? In this September 10, 2023 message, Pastor Dave Coke preaches a timely Labor Day sermon from John 6:22–27, unpacking five biblical points on labor, the God-given power to create wealth, and why Jesus Christ must be our greatest treasure above all earthly riches.

---

Five Points Covered in This Message

- Labor is a blessing from God, not a curse — and why that distinction changes everything
- God is the one who gives the power to make wealth — Deuteronomy 8:18 explained
- Wealth is not a sin — but the love of it is — and the critical difference between the two
- Jesus is to be our true riches — what Moses chose over the treasures of Egypt
- We are admonished to do all things for the glory of God

---

Key Topics and Highlights

- John 6:22–27 — Jesus rebukes the crowd for seeking Him only for bread and not for eternal life, and what that exposes about human priorities today
- Luke 16:1–13 — The Parable of the Unrighteous Manager and what Jesus teaches about using wealth shrewdly for eternal purposes
- Why the sons of this age are often more resourceful than the sons of light — and what the church should learn from that
- Genesis 2:19–20 — the very first job God gave Adam was naming every living creature, and why that matters
- Genesis 3:17 — God cursed the ground, not Adam — work itself was never the curse
- Ecclesiastes 9:10 — whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might
- Mark 6:3 — Jesus was known as the Carpenter, a man with a hard-working reputation in His community
- John 4:30–38 — Jesus tells His disciples they are entering into the labors of others — the harvest is already white
- 2 Corinthians 6 and 11 — Paul's extraordinary catalog of labors, beatings and hardships as a model of Christian work ethic
- 2 Thessalonians 3:6–10 — Paul's firm rule: if anyone is not willing to work, he should not eat
- Why Paul worked as a tentmaker in Ephesus for two years — and the remarkable result that all of Asia heard the gospel
- Deuteronomy 8:18 — it is God who gives you the power to make wealth, not your own strength alone
- The biblical building blocks of capitalism — and why profit is not a dirty word
- Job, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob — some of the greatest saints in Scripture were also among the wealthiest men of their generation
- The surprising historical connection between the Industrial Revolution, Charles Finney, David Livingstone and the explosion of foreign missions
- Malachi 3:10 — bring the whole tithe and test God on His promise to open the windows of heaven
- Why sin is never a thing or an object — sin is always a motive of the heart, and why that truth liberates people
- First Timothy 6:2–10 — godliness with contentment is great gain, and the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil
- Ananias and Sapphira — the love of money as the root of their downfall in Acts 4
- Hebrews 11:24–26 — Moses chose the reproach of Christ over all the treasures of Egypt
- Matthew 6:24 — you cannot serve both God and wealth, and why that is ultimately a matter of the heart

---

Are you passing the test? In this powerful message, Pastor Dave Coke unpacks one of the most sobering and liberating truths in all of Scripture — every single thing that happens in your life is a test from God designed to reveal what is truly in your heart. From the wilderness wanderings of Israel to Daniel's bold stand in Babylon, from Paul's challenge in 2 Corinthians to the quiet decisions of your daily life, God is always watching, always weighing, and always calling you higher.
This is not a message about fear — it is a message about clarity. When you understand that everything is a test, your whole life comes into focus.

🔥 Highlights:
    • 2 Corinthians 13:5 — Examine yourself: Paul's urgent command to test yourself and see whether you are truly in the faith. Most people want God to prove Himself to them — but God calls us to prove ourselves to Him. Self-examination is not optional for the serious believer; it is the ongoing work of the Christian life
    • Manna in the wilderness — Deuteronomy 8: God fed Israel with manna not merely to sustain them physically but to humble them and test them — to discover what was in their hearts. Would they trust Him one day at a time? Would they obey when the provision looked strange and the instructions seemed inconvenient? The wilderness was never just geography — it was a classroom
    • Daniel's test — Daniel 1: Surrounded by the most powerful empire on earth and offered the king's own food and wine, Daniel resolved in his heart that he would not defile himself. He did not wait until the pressure was on to decide what he believed — he had already settled it. Daniel's test was not primarily about diet; it was about whether the approval of God outweighed the approval of men
    • Every life circumstance is a test: Job losses, health crises, difficult relationships, financial pressure, seasons of blessing, seasons of suffering — none of it is random. God is not watching passively. He is examining what rises to the surface when life squeezes you. What comes out of you when things get hard is what was already inside you
    • Passing the test leads to promotion: Throughout Scripture, those who passed their tests were entrusted with more — Joseph, Moses, David, Daniel. The test is not punishment; it is preparation. God does not promote the untested

videos.title: Brother Bill - Does God Forgive Without Repentance? | Justice, Mercy & Prayer
videos.description:
Join Brother Bill at Living Faith Church in Rockton, Illinois for this deeply interactive sermon that tackles one of the most misunderstood topics in Christian faith: Does forgiveness require repentance — and if so, what does that mean for how we forgive others?

Opening with a pastoral follow-up to a congregant's honest question from the previous week, Brother Bill draws a careful distinction between having a *heart of forgiveness* (which we are always called tohe *completion of forgiveness* (which requires repentance from the offender). He challenges the common practice of publicly declaring forgiveness toward unrepentant criminals, arguing that even God Himself does not forgive without repentance — and neither should we confuse willingness to forgive with pretending forgiveness has occurred.

The sermon also continues Brother Bill's multi-part series on prayer, reinforcing that effective prayer requires fervency, righteousness, right motives, and alignment with God's will. Along the way, the congregation dives into sins of presumption versus ignorance, Jesus's words from the cross, the death penalty, compassion for the condemned, and what it means to pray as intimate communication with a loving Father rather than treating God like a vending machine.

**Sermon Highlights:**
• ⚖️ Does God forgive without repentance? Why the answer reshapes how we think about forgiveness
• 💔 The difference between a *heart of forgiveness* and *completed forgiveness* — and why both matter
• ✝️ "Forgive them, for they know not what they do" — what Jesus actually meant from the cross
• 🔍 Sins of presumption vs. sins of ignorance — a key Old Testament distinction that still applies
• 🗡️ The death penalty, justice, and having compassion for the condemned
• 🙏 Prayer series continued: why prayer is intimacy with God, not a vending machine
• 🏛️ Brother Bill on the Socratic method — why early church services probably looked like this discussion
• 💬 Honest, unscripted congregational dialogue on guilt, conscience, and the weight of sin
